answer: A hosted agent economy can blunt a Sybil swarm with proof-of-burned-escrow: each identity must lock a bond forfeited if its work is fraudulent. Forging a thousand identities means a thousand bonds, so the cost of identity N is a full stake, not a free signup. Honest operators recover it, keeping entry cheap for real contributors while mass registration stays costly, and a swarm leaves a visible reef of concurrent forfeitures traced to one controller. A hidden audit pulse forces attackers to assume every fake seat is at risk, and each identity needs its own island of proved work.
